projects.title: Skill4Win
projects.description: A universal, fully-brandable technique-training shell built for my 9-year-old son's basketball practice: curated YouTube reference videos side by side with his own filmed attempts, a keep-everything dated filmstrip as the progression timeline, and opt-in goals with confetti record celebrations he logs himself — no login, no PIN. The code contains zero basketball and zero Keila KK: every brand element (name, logo, icon, colors, fonts) and every drill is data authored from a PIN-gated admin, proven by a gate that deploys a blank copy and rebuilds it into a different sport without touching code.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Drizzle ORM, canvas-confetti, YouTube IFrame API (nocookie embeds with real playback-rate control), Playwright (194-check E2E battery at 375/1440/1920), theme-driven Google Fonts loading (Archivo + Open Sans as the shipped default)
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (drills, attempts, goals, one theme row that IS the entire brand), Cloudflare R2 (presigned direct uploads, zero-egress video playback, trash/ prefix with 30-day lifecycle instead of hard deletes), Vercel (hosting, force-dynamic so a DB rebrand re-skins live with no redeploy)
stack.howItWorks: The comparison is the product: one reference player beside one attempt player, 0.25×/0.5× slow-motion on both, filmstrip taps swapping clips in place. Phone videos go straight to R2 via presigned PUT (Vercel never touches the bytes) with a client-canvas thumbnail; the athlete's result logging is deliberately PIN-free while every curator mutation is server-checked. Theme colors and fonts become CSS custom properties on <html>, so /seaded can turn the whole deployment into a tennis app — new name, logo, palette, typography — in one save, and a blank copy (SEED_CONTENT=none) starts genuinely empty for the next sport.

projects.title: Prindipesa
projects.description: An Estonian-only 3D-model discovery "nest" built for my 10-year-old son: he types whatever he's obsessed with (misspellings welcome — the AI corrects "Roadblocks" to Roblox), and a manually-triggered Claude Code hunt browses six model platforms in a live browser, kid-filters ruthlessly, and serves ~6 curated models per topic as cards with one Estonian sentence and a difficulty badge each. Hearts become his print wishlist for the day his saved-up printer arrives; a built-in curriculum unlocks module by module as he grows from browser to builder.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Drizzle ORM, Playwright (hunt scraping + full E2E battery), react-markdown, Archivo Black + Archivo + Space Mono (outlined-path wordmark SVGs regenerated from a font-fallback design defect)
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (keywords, sources, models, favorites, loop-maintained lessons; EU region with Vercel functions pinned to fra1 beside it), Loop Control Center (manual-only prindipesa-ingest trigger), Vercel (hosting, installable PWA)
stack.howItWorks: The app never scrapes — it only reads the DB, so it works fully between hunts. The owner-triggered loop is the sole writer: it corrects the kid's raw keywords phonetically, live-browses MakerWorld/Printables/Thingiverse/Thangs/MyMiniFactory/Cults3D (fresh browser per query where rate limits demand), drops weapons/NSFW/horror before anything touches the database, curates across sources for beginner printability over raw popularity, and ships every card with a direct source link and a same-origin thumbnail proxy that survives hotlink-blocking CDNs.

projects.title: VAIB-X
projects.description: An X-bookmarks + YouTube idea vault: saved posts and playlist videos become action-ready "work order" cards for Claude Code. A live-browser harvest reads the owner's real X session (no API, no keys, €0), yt-dlp pulls playlist videos with full transcripts, and an in-session enrichment loop sorts everything into five categories with honest verdicts — already-adopted, obsolete, trial-worthy — plus a copy-paste launch prompt per card. The gallery wears VAIB's archival print-paper design system; the corpus was analyzed before the product was designed, and the taxonomy it proposed got overruled by the evidence.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Drizzle ORM, Playwright (embed screenshots + E2E click-through), yt-dlp (playlist diff + auto-caption transcripts), IBM Plex Mono + Libre Caslon Text
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (single bookmarks table, pending/analyzed/failed ledger), Cloudflare R2 (tweet screenshots rendered via X's public embed endpoint), chrome-devtools-live MCP (GraphQL capture from the owner's logged-in Chrome), Loop Control Center (three manual triggers: full / X-only / YouTube-only), Vercel (hosting)
stack.howItWorks: The harvest hooks fetch/XHR inside the owner's real browser tab and captures X's own GraphQL responses while auto-scrolling — bypassing the paid API and login walls entirely — while YouTube arrives keylessly through yt-dlp with transcripts stored as machine-readable deep capture; a Claude Code session then enriches each item against the owner's actual 40-project setup, so cards say "already adopted" or "rebuild this custom" instead of generic summaries, consumable via keyless JSON API, a /vault skill, or one-click copy.

projects.title: VAIB
projects.description: A front-end taste vault: paste links to well-designed websites and a Claude Code analysis loop standardizes each one into a reproduction-grade design system — DOM-extracted typography, hex palette, spacing, motion, plus a prompt-ready brief — grouped into aesthetic families and consumed by builder AI through MCP or one-click copy. The archival print-paper UI is a deliberate carbon copy of the tool that inspired it, and the vault's first analyzed entry is itself.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Drizzle ORM, mcp-handler + zod, Playwright (analysis extraction + 60+ E2E checks), IBM Plex Mono + Libre Caslon Text
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (families + entries with a pending/analyzed/failed/reanalyze ledger), Vercel Blob (hero + full-page screenshots), Loop Control Center (manual vaib-analyze loop), MCP at /api/mcp (keyless read-only tools for builder agents), Vercel (hosting), PWA share target (Android capture)
stack.howItWorks: Capture is one paste (or phone Share → VAIB); entries wait in a status ledger until the owner triggers the analysis loop, which visits each site with Playwright, extracts computed-style ground truth (real hex values, font stacks, transition curves — never eyeballed from screenshots), composes the design system + aesthetic family, and writes everything back through a key-gated API. Future builds then pull direction natively: an MCP tool call returns the full design system of any vaulted site, making the vault standing equipment in every coding session.

projects.title: Category PRO
projects.description: A web rebuild of the dead Aldata Range Manager category-management suite — a centimeter-true, sales-connected planogram editor for retail shelf planning. Seeded with real 2016 Nielsen beer data (1,258 SKUs, 36k sales facts, 355 product images), it renders bay, cooler and pallet fixtures, overlays live sales heat and share-of-space vs share-of-sales on every edit, and exports presentation-grade PNGs. Built as slice 1 of a real consulting product, not a prototype.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, SVG canvas (cm-true, 1cm = 3.1px), zustand + immer patch-based undo, Drizzle ORM, ExcelJS + PapaParse (client-side parsing), @resvg/resvg-js (server PNG export), Archivo + IBM Plex Mono
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (12-table schema: relational sales facts + JSONB planogram documents with version snapshots), Cloudflare R2 (product images), Clerk (auth), Sentry (monitoring), Vercel (hosting)
stack.howItWorks: Planograms are JSONB documents whose positions store only product + geometry — sales metrics are never frozen in, always joined live against the planogram context (account × dataset), so switching from Selver to Maxima re-scores every overlay instantly. A one-time Python pipeline parsed the legacy Nielsen XLS matrix and Master Space dimension files into the schema; ongoing data arrives through a 3-step upload wizard (saved mapping templates, EAN-first fuzzy-second SKU matching, all-or-nothing commits, new-product approval queue). Exports render the same document server-side through SVG → resvg at up to 4× print resolution with a title block.

projects.title: Livery
projects.description: A design system vault — the best design systems from past builds (tokens, fonts, distilled design rationale, component primitives) stored once and reused anywhere: browsed as auto-generated specimens, shared as public brand-book pages, and installed by AI coding agents through MCP, REST, or a shadcn-compatible registry (npx shadcn add @livery/fieldwork).

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Drizzle ORM, mcp-handler + zod, JSZip, Archivo + IBM Plex Mono (the vault wears its own first stored system)
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (systems, files, one-snapshot versioning, share links, hashed API keys), Cloudflare R2 (primitives/assets/hero shots), Clerk (auth, multi-tenant skeleton on the free plan), Vercel (hosting), Google Fonts (per-specimen font loading)
stack.howItWorks: The build agent curates at push time (verbatim tokens.css, app-prose-stripped decisions doc, only generic primitives) and pushes via the Livery Connect MCP; the server stays deliberately AI-free — a deterministic CSS parser derives structured token groups and W3C DTCG JSON from the stored CSS, which then power everything: click-to-copy specimen pages, library cards, public brand-book share links with llms.txt companions and revocable download packages, and a shadcn registry that installs a whole design system into any project with one command.

projects.title: Egert AI
projects.description: Personal AI builder portfolio and CV page. 45+ production apps showcased with technical depth — from barcode-scanning PWAs to multi-tenant SaaS. Redesigned using the Impeccable front-end design skill: OKLCH palette, Hanken Grotesk typography, varied section layouts, dark stack table. SMB value proposition and contact.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Hanken Grotesk font
stack.services: Vercel (hosting), Impeccable skill (front-end design system — OKLCH palette generation, brand register, reflex-reject font/layout guidance)
stack.howItWorks: Originally cloned from a reference site, then redesigned with the Impeccable Claude Code skill driving palette (pure white bg + committed amber primary in OKLCH), typography (Hanken Grotesk replacing reflex-rejected Cormorant + Outfit), and layout decisions (varied section structures instead of identical card grids). Featured projects use a split title/detail layout; the stack section uses a dark structured table; the about section includes a short SMB value proposition.

projects.title: Hinnavaht
projects.description: Personal grocery price watchdog PWA — scan the barcodes of products you actually buy and Hinnavaht follows their prices across three Estonian retail chains (Selver, Rimi, Barbora/Maxima): a deals-first vault opens with the deepest active discount on top, the product sheet lays the chains side by side cheapest-first, and a bundled push + email digest arrives only when something you follow drops ≥25%. Scan-or-nothing (no catalog, no manual entry), Estonian UI throughout.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Drizzle ORM, barcode-detector (native BarcodeDetector + ZXing-WASM ponyfill), web-push, Familjen Grotesk + Space Mono
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (products, watches, change-only price time series, digest audit), Selver Elasticsearch (live EAN resolve + batched price polls), Barbora Constructor.io search + PDP prices, Rimi via a Cloudflare Worker proxy (browser-grade headers open the bot gate), GitHub Actions (free 2×/day poll + digest cron with keepalive commit), Web Push VAPID, Resend (digest emails), Anthropic Claude Haiku (category harmonization), Clerk (auth), Sentry (client-side monitoring), Vercel (hosting)
stack.howItWorks: Scanning IS following: an on-device barcode decode resolves the EAN against Selver inline — carried products enter the 50-item vault with their first price snapshot, everything else is honestly rejected and stored nowhere. Because no other Estonian chain exposes EANs, a deterministic zero-AI matcher then links each product to Rimi and Barbora once (brand + unit-normalized size + percent-variant + full token accounting; anything uncertain stays honestly single-chain — a 28-case frozen golden set including a flavor-variant trap guards it). A GitHub Actions cron polls exactly the union of watched EANs twice a day through per-chain adapters, self-heals missing links, and writes a price row only on change; the digest engine evaluates each user cadence and sends one bundled push + email covering only currently-active drops ≥25%, deduplicated per product across chains. 60+ automated assertions including a 33-step Playwright click-through suite run against production.

projects.title: Keepr
projects.description: "Is it a keeper?" — a barcode-scanning grocery memory PWA. Scan any product at the shelf and instantly know whether past-you liked it: scanning IS adding (zero taps), the verdict answers from your own history in ~300 ms, and rating happens later with one tap from a morning push, a Sunday email, or the in-app queue. Every scan enriches a shared commons catalog that resolves Estonian grocery barcodes live at €0.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Drizzle ORM, barcode-detector (native BarcodeDetector + ZXing-WASM ponyfill), web-push, Familjen Grotesk + Space Mono
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (8 tables + 4 SQL views — commons catalog, immutable scan events, verdicts), Selver Elasticsearch + Open Food Facts (live resolve-on-scan, cached forever), Cloudflare R2 (product images, no hotlink rot), Anthropic Claude Haiku (category harmonization at write-gates only — never in the scan path), Web Push VAPID (actionable 1-tap rating notifications), Resend (weekly digest with HMAC-signed one-click rating links), Clerk (auth), Sentry (monitoring), Vercel (hosting + crons)
stack.howItWorks: On-device barcode decode fires one batched Neon query that renders the personal verdict instantly from the user's own history (rated / unrated / new-to-you, auto-added with zero taps); commons misses fan out to Selver + Open Food Facts inline, cache the product forever, copy its photo to R2 and harmonize retailer categories through a cached Haiku write-gate — rating then happens later via service-worker push action buttons and signed email links that record verdicts without opening the app, and the installable PWA keeps answering verdicts offline from its service-worker-cached shelf.

projects.title: Poland Travel Companion
projects.description: Trip companion PWA for a family's 12-day Poland road trip in a Tesla Model Y. A light map shows their exact route — grey behind, Tesla-blue ahead — with a live Model-Y puck, 85 verified worth-a-stop discoveries covering the whole route (incl. the Latvia, Lithuania and long Polish transit legs, so the live 'near you now' feed always has a break-stop) plus the planned itinerary, by-day browsing that auto-selects today, place cards that hand off to Google Maps, shared login-free 'visited' ticks + family notes synced across phones, and a toggleable Tesla Supercharger layer pinning chargers right on the route.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, MapLibre GL, Turf.js, Drizzle ORM, sharp, Vitest, Hanken Grotesk
stack.services: MapTiler (light vector tiles), Cloudflare R2 (place photos — Wikimedia Commons → sharp WebP), Neon PostgreSQL (shared login-free visited/notes), OSRM (route reconstruction from 21 waypoints), Wikimedia Commons API (photos), supercharge.info (Tesla Supercharger locations), Vercel (hosting)
stack.howItWorks: A build pipeline merges 104 places (85 researched discoveries + 19 planned stops extracted from the family's itinerary xlsx) and reconstructs the driving polyline from 21 Google-Maps waypoints via OSRM. The MapLibre map draws that route and splits it into covered (grey) vs ahead (Tesla-blue) at the live GPS position using Turf nearestPointOnLine + index slicing, with a Model-Y puck and planned/discovery pins. A 'near you now' sheet lists the nearest stops; tapping any pin or row opens a place card with hours, price, kid-fit, Tesla-charging notes and a 'Take me here' Google Maps deep link. Visited ticks and family notes write to Neon with no login (one shared trip, per-field upsert, refetch-on-focus so a second phone stays in sync). Photos are fetched from Wikimedia Commons, optimised with sharp to under 200KB WebP, served from R2; it's an installable PWA that caches the shell + data for brief dropouts. A build step pulls the Tesla Supercharger network from supercharge.info and keeps only sites within 10km of the route (Turf pointToLineDistance), rendering them as toggleable Tesla-red pins whose popups show power, stalls, distance off-route and a Maps deep link.

projects.title: Keeletark
projects.description: "Grammarly for Estonian." Its core is a dual-layer check where two engines work together: the estnltk MCP flags deterministic grammar/spelling/case errors as ground truth, while Claude Opus 4.8 proposes naturalness fixes — and every Claude suggestion is re-validated through estnltk before it ever reaches you, so the LLM never gets the last word. On top of that: pick-and-choose fixes, animated quality scores, English→Estonian translation, and a one-click full rewrite.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Drizzle ORM, Clerk, @anthropic-ai/sdk (Claude Opus 4.8), Vitest, Geist font
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (saved documents, glossary terms, correction events), estnltk MCP (estonian-mcp.fly.dev — deterministic Estonian spelling/grammar/case/punctuation, the ground truth), Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8 (naturalness suggestions, EN→ET translation, full-document rewrites), Clerk (invite-only auth), Vercel (hosting)
stack.howItWorks: As you type, one analyze pass runs estnltk (red correctness errors) and Claude (blue naturalness suggestions) in parallel on the same text — every Claude replacement is re-validated through estnltk (the deterministic judge) before display, red wins on overlap, and Üldskoor/Õigsus/Loomulikkus scores animate up. Fix/Skip apply surgically with single-level undo; a separate one-click Rewrite streams a full-document Claude rewrite in a chosen style (Neutral/Formal/Friendly/Concise) with before/after Accept/Discard. English input is translated to Estonian first so estnltk only ever sees Estonian. Drafts autosave to localStorage (survive navigation/refresh), a glossary of protected terms is kept verbatim, and finished pieces save to a personal archive with before→after score deltas.

projects.title: Launchpad
projects.description: Personal quick-access dashboard for all live projects. Dense visual grid with screenshots, live search filtering, dark/light mode, and keyboard shortcuts. One tile per project, one click to launch — a speed-dial cockpit for 45+ apps, synced from the portfolio on command.

stack.builtWith: HTML, CSS (custom properties, CSS Grid), vanilla JavaScript — zero dependencies, no build step
stack.services: Vercel (static hosting, auto-deploy from GitHub)
stack.howItWorks: A static single-page dashboard loads project data from a local JSON file, renders a responsive CSS Grid of screenshot tiles with clickable link chips, and filters instantly via client-side search. Screenshots batch-captured by Puppeteer. A /launchpad skill diffs the portfolio page, adds new projects, captures their screenshots, and redeploys.

projects.title: Athlon
projects.description: Estonian sports site that aggregates athletes' and teams' own Facebook posts into one clean, recency-ordered feed — full content read on Athlon, with a direct link to the original post and its original Facebook date on every entry. Fed by an operator-run, attended local-browser ingestion loop that re-hosts images to R2 and dedups posts into a Neon ledger. 33 tracked entities (incl. team Kalev/Cramo); first scrape pulled 116 posts with re-hosted images.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 14, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Drizzle ORM, sharp, Vitest (61 tests), Estonian UI
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (athletes/teams, posts ledger, per-athlete image pool, ingestion runs), Cloudflare R2 (post images re-hosted as WebP — FB CDN URLs expire), chrome-devtools MCP (attended logged-in Facebook scraping — local only, never on Vercel), Loop Control Center (attended ~2×/week loop schedule), Federated EUDI Tracker Admin (roster + run history), Vercel (hosting, ISR revalidate=60)
stack.howItWorks: An operator-run, attended local-browser loop drives a logged-in Chrome through each tracked athlete's and team's Facebook page, extracts their own posts (full text via 'See more' expansion, skipping reels and others' wall posts) and one content image. A deterministic persist step normalizes each permalink to a stable hash, dedups against the Neon ledger, inserts new posts, re-hosts the image to R2 as WebP, and logs the run. The public Next.js site reads Neon via ISR and renders a recency feed (ordered by ingest sequence, since Facebook scrambles logged-in timestamps) with sport/athlete filters, team TIIM badges, image-pool rotation, full-post pages, and — on every entry — a direct 'Vaata Facebookis' link to the cleaned original-post URL plus the original Facebook posting date.

projects.title: SongDrop — Live Request Platform
projects.description: Productized multi-tenant SaaS version of SongDrop. DJs sign up, claim their link, connect YouTube, and customize their page (profile picture, tagline, accent); guests scan a QR, search, and requests drop straight into the DJ's playlist. Self-serve onboarding, a live gig dashboard, and Stripe subscriptions — with strict per-DJ data isolation. A dedicated marketing landing page introduces the product and funnels new DJs into sign-up.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Drizzle ORM, Clerk v7, Stripe, AWS SDK S3 (R2), FastAPI, Python, Vitest + pytest, Bebas Neue + Inter fonts
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (accounts, dj_profiles, youtube_connections, requests, search_cache), Clerk (DJ auth + ownership), Google OAuth 2.0 + YouTube Data API v3 (per-DJ playlist writes), FastAPI on Render (ytmusicapi search + playlist insert), Cloudflare R2 (avatar/hero uploads), Stripe (subscriptions — €12/mo, 14-day trial), Vercel (hosting)
stack.howItWorks: Three strict identity layers — Clerk user (account) → dj_profile (tenant) → youtube_connection (Google grant) — with every mutation's ownership resolved server-side from the Clerk userId, never a client-supplied id. New DJs self-serve: claim a slug, connect YouTube via a signed-state OAuth flow (CSRF-safe; per-profile refresh token encrypted AES-256-GCM and shared with FastAPI), pick/create a playlist, and set avatar/tagline/accent (R2 uploads rendered additively on the guest page). Guests at /[slug] search YouTube Music and tap Request — Next.js inserts a row and proxies to FastAPI which inserts via YouTube Data API. Stripe Checkout (subscription mode) + Customer Portal + lifecycle webhooks drive each account's plan_status. The original single-DJ SongDrop stays live and untouched on separate infrastructure.

projects.title: Mindloop
projects.description: Private voice-to-second-brain. Press your phone's Action Button, talk — an iOS Shortcut POSTs the thought straight into a database. A weekly Claude Code synthesis then surfaces your themes, the connections between them, and the recurring "loops" you keep circling, on a responsive knowledge-graph dashboard with a live capture inbox showing each thought land and get synthesized. No inbox, no friction — press, speak, done.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Drizzle ORM, Clerk, Zod, Vitest, Fraunces + Plus Jakarta Sans + JetBrains Mono fonts
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (captures, themes, thoughts, connections, loops, runs), Vercel (hosting + token-secured POST /api/capture endpoint), Clerk (email auth), iOS Shortcuts + Wispr Flow (voice capture → HTTPS POST), Claude Code (in-session weekly synthesis brain)
stack.howItWorks: Dictate a raw thought on your phone (Wispr Flow); an iOS Shortcut bound to the Action Button POSTs it as JSON to a bearer-token-secured /api/capture route that inserts one row into Neon — no email, no inbox, empty dictations rejected server-side. A weekly Claude Code loop reads unprocessed captures, atomizes them into thoughts, writes per-theme syntheses, draws connections, and resurfaces the recurring open 'loops' you keep circling, writing it all back to Neon for a knowledge-graph dashboard. A 'Recent captures' section shows each capture with its processed/unprocessed status, and the whole dashboard collapses cleanly to a mobile layout.

projects.title: SongDrop — Guest Request Page
projects.description: QR-driven song request app for party guests. Scan → search YouTube Music → preview → tap Request → track drops into the DJ's playlist instantly. Mobile-first, one-handed, no login. Branded per-DJ hero with grayscale scanline treatment, glassmorphism search, result cards with Preview/Request split buttons, toast confirmation.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, next-themes, Drizzle ORM, Vitest, Bebas Neue + Inter fonts
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (DJs, requests, search_cache — shared with dashboard), FastAPI on Render (YouTube Music search via ytmusicapi + playlist writes via YouTube Data API v3), Vercel (hosting + API routes + OAuth), Google OAuth 2.0 (DJ YouTube connect)
stack.howItWorks: Guest scans a QR code → lands on /[slug]. 400ms debounced search proxies through Next.js API to FastAPI which queries ytmusicapi (1.5s throttle lock, persistent Neon cache with 24h TTL). Result cards show thumbnail, title, artist, duration, explicit badge. Tap Request → Next.js inserts a pending row in Neon, proxies to FastAPI /add which inserts via YouTube Data API playlistItems.insert (50 quota units, insert-level dedup). Card flips to '✓ The DJ's got it 🎧' + toast. Preview embeds YouTube IFrame inline. Pause state polled every 10s.

projects.title: SongDrop — DJ Dashboard
projects.description: DJ's command center for managing song requests at gigs. Live feed with 5-second polling, Pause/Resume toggle, QR code generation for table cards, Open Playlist link, feed density toggle (Comfortable/Compact), and 'New Gig' reset that clears both the DB feed and the YouTube playlist. Session-gated via OAuth cookie.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, next-themes, Drizzle ORM, Bebas Neue + Inter fonts
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (DJs, requests — shared with guest page), FastAPI on Render (/clear-playlist endpoint for New Gig reset), Vercel (hosting + session-gated API routes), YouTube Data API v3 (playlist clear via playlistItems.list + delete)
stack.howItWorks: Session cookie set at OAuth callback gates all /api/dj/* routes. Feed endpoint returns latest 100 requests with metadata. Dashboard polls every 5s, renders feed rows with thumbnail, title, artist, requester name (accent-colored for shout-outs), relative timestamp, and status dot. Pause toggle flips djs.paused — guest page reflects within 10s. New Gig deletes all request rows (resets dedup) AND empties the YouTube playlist via FastAPI (paginated list + individual delete, 50 quota units per track, guard at 100). QR panel generates from guest URL with Copy Link + Download QR.

projects.title: Saku Tenniseklubi
projects.description: Production website + custom weekly-grid booking system for an Estonian clay-court tennis club (live client work). Public site with CMS-driven content, interactive booking calendar with request flow, and a full admin panel — 8 management sections, drag-select/move/resize grid, request inbox with approve/reject, closures, recurring series, and 6 content editors. 71 tests, DST-safe timezone engine, Resend email notifications. Deployed and handed over to client.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Drizzle ORM, Vitest, Luxon, Clerk, Zod, sharp, Newsreader + Geist + JetBrains Mono fonts
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (multi-tenant — 9 tables: tenants, tenant_admins, courts, booking_blocks, booking_requests, recurring_series, announcements, gallery_items, price_rows), Cloudflare R2 (sharp-processed AVIF/WebP image CDN), Clerk (admin auth — email+password, multi-admin per tenant), Resend (booking-request notification emails to admin), Vercel (hosting + auto-deploy)
stack.howItWorks: Multi-tenant from day one — tenant resolved from request host for public reads, from authenticated Clerk user via tenant_admins join for every admin write. A single Europe/Tallinn schedule engine (Luxon, DST-safe across the October EEST→EET switch) drives both the public read-only weekly grid and the interactive admin grid from one booking_blocks table. Public visitors click free slots to submit booking requests (name/phone/email) — the slot is held as pending, admin gets a Resend notification email, then approves (auto-derives privacy-safe label like 'MartT') or rejects (frees the slot). Admin grid supports drag-select creation, click-to-edit, drag-move, and resize via custom pointer events (no DnD library) with pure-tested interaction math. Close-day creates rain/maintenance blocks with affected-booking preview. Recurring series generate DST-correct weekly blocks across the full season. Six CMS editors (homepage, Klubist, pricing, news, gallery, settings) let the admin update all public content. Images processed with sharp into responsive AVIF/WebP served from R2. 71 Vitest tests cover timezone math, schedule engine, conflicts, grid interactions, recurring generation, and label derivation.

projects.title: HankeRadar
projects.description: AI-powered construction tender matching for Estonian builders. Scrapes Hange.ee + Holt.ee, matches via Haiku 4.5, sends email + Telegram notifications. Desktop responsive with editable profiles and dual notification cadence.

stack.builtWith: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Drizzle ORM, grammy, Cheerio, Clerk v7, Fraunces + DM Sans + Epilogue + JetBrains Mono fonts
stack.services: Neon PostgreSQL (companies, trades, listings, matches), Vercel (hosting + serverless), Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5 (AI match scoring), Resend (email notifications — digest + instant), Telegram Bot API via grammy (@HankeRadarBot — instant alerts), Clerk (auth), ariregister.rik.ee (Business Register lookup), GitHub Actions (scrape cron every 2h + daily digest 7:00 UTC)
stack.howItWorks: GitHub Actions scrapes Hange.ee (paginated, ~387 listings) and Holt.ee every 2h. Location pre-filter narrows by county neighbor map with Tallinn-specific handling. Haiku 4.5 scores each listing-company pair 1-10 with Estonian reasoning. Score ≥7 triggers instant Telegram + email (Resend). Daily digest collects all unnotified matches.
